title: OSHA construction personal protective equipment practice questions
description: Free OSHA construction PPE practice questions on 29 CFR 1926 Subpart E. Every answer is explained and linked to the section it comes from.

questions.question: Under 1926.95, who pays for protective equipment used to comply with Part 1926, apart from the listed exceptions?

options.A: The employer, at no cost to employees
options.C: The employer and employee split the cost
options.D: The general contractor's insurer

questions.explanation: Except as provided in paragraphs (d)(2) through (d)(6), protective equipment used to comply with Part 1926 "shall be provided by the employer at no cost to employees."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.95, Criteria for personal protective equipment (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: the protective equipment, including personal protective equipment (PPE), used to comply with this part, shall be provided by the employer at no cost to employees.

questions.question: An employer does not have to pay for non-specialty steel-toe boots on what condition?

options.A: The employee has worked there less than 90 days
options.C: The employer permits the boots to be worn off the job site
options.D: The boots were bought before the project began

questions.explanation: The employer is not required to pay for non-specialty safety-toe footwear and non-specialty prescription safety eyewear, "provided that the employer permits such items to be worn off the job-site."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.95, Criteria for personal protective equipment (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: provided that the employer permits such items to be worn off the job-site.

questions.question: When is an employer not required to pay for replacement PPE?

options.A: When the PPE wore out from normal use
options.B: When the employee lost or intentionally damaged the PPE
options.C: When the PPE is more than one year old
options.D: When the project is shorter than 30 days

questions.explanation: "The employer must pay for replacement PPE, except when the employee has lost or intentionally damaged the PPE."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.95, Criteria for personal protective equipment (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: The employer must pay for replacement PPE, except when the employee has lost or intentionally damaged the PPE.

questions.question: Which item does 1926.95(d)(4) list as one the employer is not required to pay for?

options.D: Sunscreen used solely for protection from weather

questions.explanation: The employer is not required to pay for ordinary clothing, skin creams or other items "used solely for protection from weather," and the examples include "ordinary sunglasses, and sunscreen."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.95, Criteria for personal protective equipment (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: used solely for protection from weather, such as winter coats, jackets, gloves, parkas, rubber boots, hats, raincoats, ordinary sunglasses, and sunscreen.

questions.question: When employees provide their own protective equipment, who is responsible for assuring its adequacy, maintenance and sanitation?

options.D: The OSHA area office

questions.explanation: "Where employees provide their own protective equipment, the employer shall be responsible to assure its adequacy, including proper maintenance, and sanitation of such equipment."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.95, Criteria for personal protective equipment (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Where employees provide their own protective equipment, the employer shall be responsible to assure its adequacy, including proper maintenance, and sanitation of such equipment.

questions.question: Under 1926.95(c), PPE must be selected to ensure what?

options.A: That it is the lowest-cost option
options.B: That it properly fits each affected employee
options.D: That it is made in the United States

questions.explanation: Employers must ensure all PPE "is selected to ensure that it properly fits each affected employee," and is of safe design and construction for the work.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.95, Criteria for personal protective equipment (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Is selected to ensure that it properly fits each affected employee.

questions.question: Employees working where there is a possible danger of head injury from falling or flying objects must be protected by what?

options.D: A face shield

questions.explanation: Employees working where there is a possible danger of head injury "from impact, or from falling or flying objects, or from electrical shock and burns, shall be protected by protective helmets."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.100, Head protection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Employees working in areas where there is a possible danger of head injury from impact, or from falling or flying objects, or from electrical shock and burns, shall be protected by protective helmets.

questions.question: Head protection for employees exposed to high-voltage electric shock and burns must also meet which part of the named ANSI Z89.1 standards?

options.D: Nothing more than the general requirements

questions.explanation: For employees exposed to high-voltage electric shock and burns, head protection must also meet "Section 9.7 ("Electrical Insulation")" of one of the consensus standards listed in 1926.100(b)(1).

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.100, Head protection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: also meets the specifications contained in Section 9.7 ("Electrical Insulation") of any of the consensus standards identified in paragraph (b)(1) of this section.

questions.question: Under 1926.101, which of these is stated to be not acceptable as an ear protective device?

options.D: Ear inserts fitted by a competent person

questions.explanation: The rule says: "Plain cotton is not an acceptable protective device."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.101, Hearing protection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Plain cotton is not an acceptable protective device.

questions.question: Who must fit or determine ear protective devices that are inserted in the ear?

options.D: Competent persons, individually for each user

questions.explanation: "Ear protective devices inserted in the ear shall be fitted or determined individually by competent persons."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.101, Hearing protection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Ear protective devices inserted in the ear shall be fitted or determined individually by competent persons.

questions.question: When there is a hazard from flying objects, the eye protection used must provide what?

options.D: Laser optical density of 8

questions.explanation: The employer must ensure each affected employee uses "eye protection that provides side protection when there is a hazard from flying objects"; clip-on or slide-on side shields that meet the section are acceptable.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.102, Eye and face protection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: uses eye protection that provides side protection when there is a hazard from flying objects.

questions.question: An employee who wears prescription glasses does work with eye hazards. Which option does 1926.102 allow?

options.B: Wearing eye protection that fits over the prescription lenses without disturbing either lens's position
options.C: Skipping eye protection for tasks under one hour
options.D: Wearing contact lenses instead of eye protection

questions.explanation: The employee must wear eye protection "that incorporates the prescription in its design, or wears eye protection that can be worn over the prescription lenses without disturbing the proper position of the prescription lenses or the protective lenses."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.102, Eye and face protection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: wears eye protection that incorporates the prescription in its design, or wears eye protection that can be worn over the prescription lenses without disturbing the proper position of the prescription lenses or the protective lenses.

questions.question: What does 1926.102 say about using a welding filter shade more dense than the one listed in its Table E-1?

options.C: It may be used to suit the individual's needs
options.D: It is allowed only for soldering

questions.explanation: Table E-1 "shall be used as a guide" for selecting shade numbers, and "Shades more dense than those listed may be used to suit the individual's needs."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.102, Eye and face protection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Shades more dense than those listed may be used to suit the individual's needs.

questions.question: Where does 1926.103 say the respiratory protection requirements for construction work are set out?
questions.explanation: The note in 1926.103 says the requirements for construction work "are identical to those set forth at 29 CFR 1910.134 of this chapter."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.103, Respiratory protection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: The requirements applicable to construction work under this section are identical to those set forth at 29 CFR 1910.134 of this chapter.

questions.question: Under 1926.104, what must happen to a lanyard that has been actually subjected to in-service loading?

options.A: It is inspected and returned to service
options.C: It is used only for static load testing
options.D: It is immediately removed from service and not used again for employee safeguarding

questions.explanation: Any lifeline, safety belt or lanyard "actually subjected to in-service loading, as distinguished from static load testing, shall be immediately removed from service and shall not be used again for employee safeguarding."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.104, Safety belts, lifelines, and lanyards (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Any lifeline, safety belt, or lanyard actually subjected to in-service loading, as distinguished from static load testing, shall be immediately removed from service and shall not be used again for employee safeguarding.

questions.question: Under 1926.104, a lifeline must be secured above the point of operation to an anchorage capable of supporting a minimum dead weight of how much?

options.D: 10,000 pounds

questions.explanation: Lifelines must be secured above the point of operation "to an anchorage or structural member capable of supporting a minimum dead weight of 5,400 pounds."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.104, Safety belts, lifelines, and lanyards (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Lifelines shall be secured above the point of operation to an anchorage or structural member capable of supporting a minimum dead weight of 5,400 pounds.

questions.question: Under 1926.105, safety nets are required when workplaces are more than how high above the ground or water surface (where ladders, scaffolds, safety lines and similar means are impractical)?

options.D: 25 feet

questions.explanation: "Safety nets shall be provided when workplaces are more than 25 feet above the ground or water surface, or other surfaces where the use of ladders, scaffolds, catch platforms, temporary floors, safety lines, or safety belts is impractical."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.105, Safety nets (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Safety nets shall be provided when workplaces are more than 25 feet above the ground or water surface, or other surfaces where the use of ladders, scaffolds, catch platforms, temporary floors, safety lines, or safety belts is impractical.

questions.question: How far must a safety net extend beyond the edge of the work surface where employees are exposed?

options.D: 25 feet

questions.explanation: "Nets shall extend 8 feet beyond the edge of the work surface where employees are exposed" and may in no case be more than 25 feet below the work surface.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.105, Safety nets (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Nets shall extend 8 feet beyond the edge of the work surface where employees are exposed

questions.question: Ring buoys provided for emergency rescue over or near water must have at least how much line?

options.D: 90 feet

questions.explanation: "Ring buoys with at least 90 feet of line shall be provided and readily available for emergency rescue operations." The 200-foot figure is the maximum distance between ring buoys.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.106, Working over or near water (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Ring buoys with at least 90 feet of line shall be provided and readily available for emergency rescue operations.

questions.question: When must buoyant work vests or life preservers be inspected for defects that would alter their strength or buoyancy?

options.B: Prior to and after each use
options.D: Once a year by the manufacturer

questions.explanation: "Prior to and after each use, the buoyant work vests or life preservers shall be inspected for defects which would alter their strength or buoyancy." Defective units may not be used.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.106, Working over or near water (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Prior to and after each use, the buoyant work vests or life preservers shall be inspected for defects which would alter their strength or buoyancy.
